title: Perfect localizing generation for quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic spaces
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Algebraic spaces and schemes are [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-pc-scheme]. Use the small etale site with structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$, module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ be the full subcategory whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A perfect object means an object locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Let $S$ be a scheme and $X$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$; quasi-compact means every open cover of $|X|$ has a finite subcover and quasi-separated means its diagonal is quasi-compact. Then $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ is closed under arbitrary set-indexed coproducts computed in $D(\mathcal O_X)$, and is the smallest strictly full subcategory of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ containing the perfect objects and closed under shifts, distinguished-triangle cones, retracts and arbitrary set-indexed coproducts.

proof.text: Use the small skeleton fixed in [def-weil-size-convention]. By [lem-pur-ringed-site-grothendieck-abelian], $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ is Grothendieck; by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] it has K-injective resolutions. Its coproducts are exact: write a coproduct of short exact sequences as the filtered colimit of the finite subsum sequences. Finite subsums are exact by the abelian biproduct identities, and the filtered colimit preserves exactness by the Grothendieck property. The finite-subsums identification follows directly from the coproduct universal property: compatible maps from all finite subsums are precisely families of maps from individual summands. Apply [lem-kun-grothendieck-derived-coproducts] and [src-weil-derived-homology-preserves-coproducts]. Thus ambient derived coproducts exist and $H^q(\bigoplus_i E_i)\cong\bigoplus_iH^q(E_i)$. By [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits] the right side is quasi-coherent for $E_i\in C_X$. Fullness then restricts the ambient coproduct universal property to $C_X$, so its coproducts agree with the ambient ones.

source.place: Tag 08F3, lemma-quasi-coherence-direct-sums, proof; injectives.tex Tag 07D9, lemma-derived-products, clauses (1)-(2).

proof.text: The full subcategory $C_X$ is strictly full and shift-stable since cohomology is functorial and $H^q(E[n])=H^{q+n}(E)$. For a triangle $E\to F\to G\to E[1]$ with $E,F\in C_X$, [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] gives $0\to\operatorname{coker}(H^qE\to H^qF)\to H^qG\to\ker(H^{q+1}E\to H^{q+1}F)\to0$. The end terms are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], and the middle is so by [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-extension-closed]. Rotation gives the other two-out-of-three cases, so $C_X$ is triangulated. It is retract-closed: if $E$ is a retract of $F$, applying $H^q$ expresses $H^qE$ as the image of an idempotent of $H^qF$; image closure in [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits] applies. Finally [lem-sfb-space-perfect-objects-compact] places every perfect object in $C_X$. Hence $C_X$ itself is one of the ambient subcategories in the statement.

source.place: Tag 071X, definition-derived-quasi-coherent and the following explanation via spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1; Tag 09M8.

proof.text: Choose $P$ by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-weak-generator]; it is compact in $C_X$ by [lem-sfb-space-perfect-objects-compact]. Its shifted-Hom vanishing criterion is precisely weak generation of $C_X$: replacing $n$ by $-n$ identifies maps $P[n]\to E$ with maps $P\to E[-n]$. Apply [lem-pc-compact-generators-build-objects] to the singleton family $P$ in the triangulated category $C_X$, using the coproducts of step 1. For each $E\in C_X$ it gives a sequence $X_1\to X_2\to\cdots$, with $X_1$ and all $Z_n$ coproducts of shifts of $P$, triangles $Z_n\to X_n\to X_{n+1}\to Z_n[1]$, and the telescope triangle $\bigoplus_nX_n\xrightarrow{1-\mathrm{shift}}\bigoplus_nX_n\to E\to(\bigoplus_nX_n)[1]$. These are ambient distinguished triangles; their coproducts are ambient ones by step 1. All index sets, including the shifted-Hom indexing sets used by this lemma, lie in the chosen larger universe.

source.place: Tag 09IY, theorem-bondal-van-den-Bergh; Tag 09M8, proposition-compact-is-perfect; derived.tex Tag 09SN, lemma-write-as-colimit.

proof.text: Let $L$ be any strictly full ambient subcategory containing all perfect objects and closed under the four stated operations. It contains $P$, all its shifts, and their coproducts; hence it contains $X_1$ and each $Z_n$. Induct on $n$: from $X_n,Z_n\in L$, cone closure applied to $Z_n\to X_n$ puts $X_{n+1}$ in $L$. Thus $\bigoplus_n X_n\in L$, and its endomorphism $1-\mathrm{shift}$ has cone $E$, so $E\in L$. This proves $C_X\subseteq L$ for every such $L$. Step 2 and the coproduct closure of step 1 show that $C_X$ itself has all those properties, establishing the claimed smallest subcategory and the coproduct clause.
